question: Why are swimming times given only to the hundredth of a second when the clocks can measure thousandths?
answer: Because of the 1972 Olympic 400 m medley. Gunnar Larsson beat Tim McKee by 0.002 seconds, 4:31.981 to 4:31.983. A swimmer covers about 2 mm in a thousandth of a second, less than the difference allowed in building two lanes. Since then ties at the hundredth stand, and swimmers share the medal.
move: Never report a difference finer than the ruler that produced it.
reference: Organising Committee for the Games of the XXth Olympiad, Official Report, Munich, 1974
